scenario: Runtime-task lease heartbeat fix + cross-instance in-flight SSE live delivery

defectFixed.finding: RuntimeTaskScheduler.heartbeat() had no caller and no renewal loop; any execution longer than lease-seconds was recovered as LEASE_EXPIRED with EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
defectFixed.secondaryFinding: All @Scheduled methods shared Spring Boot's default single-thread scheduler, so a blocking execution also starved the cross-instance SSE catch-up and revocation pollers.
fix: Added ExecutionHeartbeatRegistry (in-flight token registry) and LeaseHeartbeat (dedicated single-thread ScheduledExecutorService, not the model-call thread, not shared @Scheduled)
WorkspaceMultiWorkerDriver and GaMultiWorkerDriver register/unregister the claim around adapter.execute (try/finally)
On renewal failure the registry marks ownership lost and stops renewing; DB conditional renewal stays the authority
spring.task.scheduling.pool.size=4 so scheduled convergence paths are not starved by a blocking execution
defectFixed.noMigration: lease_until / heartbeat_at already exist; behaviour fix only, no data-format or security-boundary change

scenarios.name: long execution survives the lease via heartbeat
scenarios.note: same 6s-fixture run previously produced LEASE_EXPIRED; with the fix it completes honestly

scenarios.name: cross-instance in-flight SSE live delivery
scenarios.finding: The run was executed by A while the SSE connection lived on B; B delivered live deltas and the terminal event via the DB-cursor catch-up poller (1s interval). Sequence numbers are contiguous with no gap or duplicate.

scenarios.name: cursor reconnect (Last-Event-ID)
scenarios.finding: Reconnect from cursor 2 replays exactly the events after the cursor and no earlier ones

regression.focusedCommand: testNonLive --tests com.specagent.runtime.execution.* --tests com.specagent.agent.runtime.* --tests com.specagent.assistant.runtime.* --tests com.specagent.architecture.* bootJar

liveWorkerIdLogging: WorkerPollingGate now logs the per-process worker UUID so runtime_tasks.worker_id can be mapped to an instance (design §9); the OIDC /api/health redaction is unchanged
limitations: Native model output is a deterministic test-only fixture; not real-provider qualification
Production defaults are lease 60s / heartbeat 10s; the acceptance used 15s/3s so a single blocking fragment exceeds the lease quickly
No revocation, slow-client, kill-process takeover, DB-outage or fleet key rotation/rollback acceptance in this scenario
The 6s fixture delay is an acceptance setting, not a capacity claim
